the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences, recent intent, and multiple latent interests. [Hierarchical long and short-term preference modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) uses dynamic routing to extract multiple long-term interest vectors, self-attention for recent interactions, and similarity-based matching with time encoding to fuse them. [MIMAR-SRec (AAAI 2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models intentions across contextual windows, combining intent prototypes, contrastive learning, and robustness to interaction and temporal noise.

The closest match to candidate-conditioned scoring is [D2MFRec (published December 2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z): soft clustering extracts K interest vectors; target-item embeddings determine attention weights over those vectors. A separate Transformer/recent-history branch captures global and short-term preferences, with learned gating and denoising contrastive objectives. Candidate-dependent aggregation allows the same history to produce different representations for different candidate items.

Practical inference for this benchmark: retain SASRec’s contextual sequence states, add a small bank of learned interest queries and a recent-window branch, then use each candidate embedding to attend over the resulting interest vectors. Gate this score with the original final-state score; optionally incorporate timestamp gaps into attention or routing. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated benchmark gains. Ablate multi-interest pooling, candidate conditioning, and temporal fusion separately using macro validation HR@10. Cache interest vectors and score catalog items in chunks for full-catalog recommendations; single-GPU feasibility and improvements require measurement.

---

Sampled BCE is a plausible SASRec bottleneck, but calibration and ranking gains are distinct. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) links negative sampling to overconfidence and motivates generalized BCE with multiple negatives. [Sampled-softmax research (2024)](https://zlstwebsite.github.io/Zlst/publication/on-the-effectiveness-of-sampled-softmax-loss-for-item-recommendation/) identifies informative hard-negative gradients and benefits for top-K ranking and long-tail recommendation. Practical ablation: retain SASRec, compare baseline BCE, multi-negative generalized BCE, and sampled softmax. For nonuniform sampling, treat proposal correction explicitly; [RecSys 2025’s LogQ repository](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) provides implementations comparing uniform, in-batch, mixed, and corrected objectives.

Harder negatives need controlled difficulty. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports problems from introducing hard negatives early; it combines uniform warm-start, global candidate recall, and curriculum re-ranking. It discusses stochastic selection among top-ranked candidates and uncertainty-based downweighting as ways to mitigate false negatives. Highest-scoring unseen items are not verified negatives. A practical hypothesis is uniform warm-up followed by a mixture of uniform and moderately hard negatives, excluding observed training positives; do not infer negative labels from unavailable ratings or exposure data.

Evidence does not establish an Electronics-specific improvement. [A 2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds substantial sampler-dependent head/mid/tail tradeoffs that aggregate metrics can conceal. Compare objectives and negative counts under matched GPU time using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; report category results alongside it. Electronics’ lower-tail margins are diagnostic signals, not evidence of better held-out ranking.

---

Recent work supports combining temporal sequence modeling with item graphs. [TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) combines global temporal item transitions, time-interval-aware Transformers and graph contrastive learning—components compatible with training from interaction histories without pretrained language weights. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734) emphasizes that complements can exhibit both relevance and dissimilarity, so similarity alone is insufficient. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) offers a simpler alternative: infer complementary recommendations through directed, weighted projections of user–item interactions. Its query-item task differs from personalized next-item prediction; reported gains do not establish gains on this benchmark.

The closest architectural precedent, [SCG-SPRe (2021/2022)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3464302), uses separate substitute/complement graphs and candidate-dependent temporal kernels. It assumes relation graphs, which are unavailable here. A feasible adaptation hypothesis: retain SASRec, add sparse training-only transition graphs across time windows, encode titles/descriptions using TF-IDF or randomly initialized token embeddings, and learn a gate combining sequence, text-similarity and transition scores. Treat graph channels as latent associations: co-purchase does not prove complementarity, textual similarity does not prove substitution, and histories do not observe fulfilled needs or compatibility. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec encodes interaction histories using item and learned positional embeddings, causal self-attention, and feed-forward blocks. It scores candidates by dot product with the final sequence representation, sharing input/output item embeddings. Training uses next-item supervision and sampled binary cross-entropy. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
